context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system processes card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud within a sub-50ms latency window while providing case management for analysts. It operates within AWS (`eu-west-1`) to meet PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 7-year tamper-evident audit requirement on a fixed budget.

## Key Elements
* **Payment Gateway / Acquiring System**: External actor submitting authorization requests.
* **Fraud Analyst & Risk Operations Manager**: Internal users reviewing cases and updating rules.
* **Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System**: Core software system hosted on AWS.
* **AWS API Gateway / Envoy Proxy**: Edge layer handling mTLS termination and traffic routing.
* **AWS Fargate**: Containerized microservices executing fraud scoring and business logic.
* **AWS Cognito**: Managed Identity Provider handling OIDC/OAuth2 authentication and RBAC.
* **AWS S3 Object Lock**: Immutable storage backend configured in Compliance Mode for audit logging.
* **AWS KMS**: Cryptographic service managing envelope encryption and hardware-isolated keys.

## Relationships
* **Payment Gateway** to **AWS API Gateway**: Submits payment authorization requests via **gRPC over mTLS**.
* **Fraud Analysts** to **AWS Cognito / Web Frontend**: Authenticates via **OIDC/OAuth2 over HTTPS/REST**.
* **Core Fargate Services** to **AWS S3 Object Lock**: Archives scoring inputs and decisions via **AWS SDK (HTTPS)**.
* **External Fraud Intelligence Feeds** to **Core System**: Ingests risk data via **HTTPS/REST webhooks**.

## Technology Stack
* **AWS Fargate & API Gateway**: Chosen for serverless container orchestration to meet the 3,000 TPS at <50ms P99 SLA without managing Kubernetes.
* **gRPC over mTLS**: Selected for low-overhead, high-throughput service communication and PCI-DSS transport security.
* **AWS Cognito**: Offloads identity management to reduce operational toil for a 3-engineer team.
* **AWS S3 Object Lock (Compliance Mode)**: Implemented to mathematically guarantee 7-year immutability for regulatory auditability.
* **AWS KMS / CloudHSM**: Provides hardware-accelerated encryption and tokenization to minimize PCI-DSS scope.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages managed AWS services to remain strictly within the €25k monthly budget and operational capacity of a 3-engineer team while satisfying strict PCI-DSS Level 1 security and 7-year auditability mandates. Edge offloading and serverless compute guarantee sub-50ms latency at high throughput without requiring self-managed infrastructure.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
- Screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time while providing case management for analysts.
- Ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, sub-50ms P99 decision latency, and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a strict budget.

## Key Elements
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System [system, context]
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Operations Manager [person, context]
- Payment Gateway / Acquiring System [externalSystem, context]
- External Fraud Intelligence Feeds [externalSystem, context]
- AWS API Gateway / Envoy Proxy [externalSystem, context]
- Scoring Service Container [container, Go / AWS Fargate]
- Case Management Container [container, Node.js / TypeScript / AWS Fargate]
- Amazon ElastiCache for Redis [container, in-memory cache]
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 [container, relational database]
- AWS S3 Object Lock [externalSystem, storage]
- AWS Cognito [externalSystem, auth]
- AWS KMS [externalSystem, security]

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Acquiring System -> AWS API Gateway / Envoy Proxy (gRPC over mTLS)
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Operations Manager -> AWS Cognito (OIDC/OAuth2 over HTTPS/REST)
- AWS API Gateway / Envoy Proxy -> Scoring Service Container (gRPC)
- Scoring Service Container -> Amazon ElastiCache for Redis (RESP over TLS)
- Scoring Service Container -> AWS S3 Object Lock (AWS SDK / HTTPS)
- Case Management Container -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 (PostgreSQL wire protocol over TLS)
- External Fraud Intelligence Feeds -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System (HTTPS/REST webhooks)

## Technology Stack
- **Go (Golang)** on **AWS Fargate**: Selected for the Scoring Service Container to guarantee predictable low memory footprint and sub-50ms P99 latency.
- **Node.js / TypeScript** on **AWS Fargate**: Powers the Case Management Container for analyst workflows and UI rendering.
- **Amazon ElastiCache for Redis**: Provides in-memory feature storage and hot rules caching for sub-millisecond lookups.
- **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2**: Persists case management metadata and review actions securely.
- **AWS S3 Object Lock**: Enforces Compliance Mode for immutable, tamper-evident 7-year audit logging.
- **AWS KMS**: Manages envelope encryption, database column encryption, and customer-managed keys (CMKs).
- **AWS Cognito & AWS Secrets Manager**: Handle OIDC/OAuth2 authentication, RBAC, and dynamic secret rotation.

## Rationale
- Container isolation separates the high-throughput scoring hot path from analyst workflows, protecting performance and PCI-DSS boundaries.
- Managed AWS services and lean microservices architectures enable a 3-engineer team to operate reliably under the €25,000 monthly budget.

## Overview
[Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System] screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real time while providing case management for fraud analysts. It is operated by three engineers within a fixed €25,000/monthly AWS infrastructure budget while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Key Elements
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System (System)
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Operations Manager (Person)
- Payment Gateway / Acquiring System (External System)
- External Fraud Intelligence Feeds (External System)
- AWS API Gateway / Envoy Proxy (External System)
- AWS Fargate (External System)
- AWS Cognito (External System)
- AWS S3 Object Lock (External System)
- AWS KMS (External System)
- Scoring Service Container (Container - Go / AWS Fargate)
  - API Handler Component
  - Scoring Engine Component
  - Audit Dispatcher Component
  - Circuit Breaker & Fallback Manager Component
- Case Management Container (Container - Node.js / TypeScript / AWS Fargate)
- Amazon ElastiCache for Redis (Container - In-memory cache)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 (Container - Relational database)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Acquiring System -> AWS API Gateway / Envoy Proxy (gRPC over mTLS)
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Operations Manager -> AWS Cognito (OIDC/OAuth2 over HTTPS/REST)
- External Fraud Intelligence Feeds -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System (HTTPS/REST webhooks)
- AWS API Gateway / Envoy Proxy -> Scoring Service Container (gRPC over mTLS)
- Scoring Service Container -> Amazon ElastiCache for Redis (RESP over TLS)
- Scoring Service Container -> AWS S3 Object Lock (AWS SDK / HTTPS)
- Case Management Container -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 (PostgreSQL wire protocol over TLS)

## Technology Stack
- Go on AWS Fargate: Selected for the Scoring Service Container to deliver predictable low memory footprint and sub-50ms P99 latency.
- Node.js / TypeScript on AWS Fargate: Powers the Case Management Container for rapid analyst UI and workflow iteration.
- Amazon ElastiCache for Redis: Provides in-memory feature storage and hot-rules caching for sub-millisecond lookups.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2: Persists case management metadata and review actions securely with auto-scaling capabilities.
- AWS S3 Object Lock: Configured in Compliance Mode for tamper-evident, 7-year audit logging.
- AWS KMS: Manages envelope encryption and Fargate ephemeral storage encryption for PCI-DSS compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture utilizes containerized microservices on AWS Fargate paired with an in-memory Redis cache to meet the strict sub-50ms P99 latency requirement at 3,000 transactions per second. Immutable storage via AWS S3 Object Lock and AWS KMS encryption ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a strict €25,000 monthly budget.

Case Management Container.analysis:
## Overview
[Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System] screens card-not-present payment authorizations of a mid-size payment processor for fraud before approval. It provides a case management container for fraud analysts to review suspicious payments while meeting strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Operations Manager [person, context]
- Case Management Container [container] (Node.js / TypeScript / AWS Fargate)
- Case Management API Component [component] (Node.js / TypeScript)
- Audit & Compliance Writer Component [component] (Node.js / TypeScript)
- Authentication & Authorization Middleware Component [component] (Node.js / TypeScript)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 [container] (relational database)
- Amazon CloudWatch [externalSystem]
- AWS Cognito [externalSystem]
- AWS S3 Object Lock [externalSystem]
- AWS KMS [externalSystem]

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Operations Manager -> Case Management API Component (HTTPS/REST over TLS)
- Authentication & Authorization Middleware Component -> AWS Cognito (OIDC/OAuth2 verification)
- Case Management API Component -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 (PostgreSQL wire protocol over TLS with AWS KMS encryption)
- Audit & Compliance Writer Component -> Amazon CloudWatch (Structured JSON over HTTPS)

## Technology Stack
- Node.js / TypeScript: Core runtime and language for the Case Management Container ensuring rapid development for a 3-engineer team.
- AWS Fargate: Serverless container execution providing automated scaling based on active analyst concurrency within budget.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2: Relational database providing column-level encryption via AWS KMS for zero PAN footprint compliance.
- AWS Cognito: Managed Identity Provider handling JWT validation, OIDC/OAuth2, and strict RBAC.
- Amazon CloudWatch: Centralized logging service capturing structured audit logs and metrics.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless AWS services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while staying within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Strict data-masking, zero-PAN footprints, and immutable audit logging ensure full PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability.
